subject: Dedicated capacity: performance acceptance criteria, measurement, and billing implications
messages:
From: Jason Turner <jturner@orbitai.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@orbitai.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity proposal / performance guarantees

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for sending the proposal. A couple of things we need to lock down before legal/procurement will move forward:

1) Measurement units: your proposal references both tokens/sec and requests/sec. For our inference mix (short chat + long-document summarization) tokens/sec is the primary metric. Can you confirm exactly which metric you would guarantee and how you translate between them?

2) Latency targets: we need a clear p50/p95 latency target per model family and sequence length bucket. The draft in the PDF is a bit high-level.

3) Acceptance testing: what does the validation run look like? Who supplies the harness? Will any test traffic be billed as committed usage or treated as validation (no charge)?

4) If Redwood does not hit the committed throughput, what is the commercial remedy? We expect either pro-rated credits or a discount path for the initial term.

Can you put something concrete in writing and share the acceptance test plan so we can circulate internally?

-Jason
Jason Turner
CTO, Orbit AI
jturner@orbitai.com
(415) 555-0193
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jason Turner <jturner@orbitai.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Procurement Team <procure@orbitai.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity proposal / performance guarantees

Jason — thanks for the clear list. Attached is a focused acceptance test plan (dedicated_acceptance_testplan.xlsx) and an annotated excerpt of the proposal (RI_Proposal_ORBIT-2026.pdf). Outline below; please let me know which items you want tightened.

Summary (short):
- Metric of record: tokens/sec (aggregate across pool) for the committed GPU pool. We will express guarantees as a sustained tokens/sec over a 60-minute rolling window (the "sustained window") at a target p95 generation latency threshold per model family. requests/sec will be used only for operational routing compatibility but not as the economic guarantee.

- Latency: p50 / p95 targets per model family and sequence-length bucket (see sheet "LatencyBands" in the test plan). Example: LlamaX-70B, seq <= 256: p95 < 220ms; seq 257-1024: p95 < 480ms. These are configurable per model in the deal.

- Measurement methodology:
  * Validation harness: Orbit supplies representative prompts and the client-side harness (recommended: k6 + our data loader), Redwood runs the harness against the Dedicated pool in your VPC peering link.
  * Duration: 72-hour soak with two 60-minute sustained windows used for acceptance (best-of-three).
  * Metrics collection: Redwood will publish a signed CSV with minute-resolution tokens/sec and per-request latencies, plus a compressed KV-cache artifact showing warm vs cold start token counts.
  * Time sync: all timestamps are in UTC; we include sequence numbering to reconcile any lost samples.

- Commercial remedies if SLA not met during acceptance:
  * If measured sustained tokens/sec < committed by >10% in both accepted windows, Redwood will offer a one-time credit equal to 10% of the first monthly invoice and a free 2-week extension of the acceptance verification window.
  * If shortfall >25%, customer may elect a 6-month reduced-rate discount (15%) on committed spend or transition to a smaller pool without penalty.

Notes / open items: whether validation traffic should be billed as part of the commitment. Our standard is to treat acceptance run usage as excluded from the first 30 days of committed billing; happy to make that explicit in the SOW.

I attached the spreadsheet with the exact test commands, example scripts, and the latency bands matrix — that should be enough for your SREs to review.

If this matches your expectations, Rishi and I will fold the language into the SOW and Soc2 addendum and send for signature.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
From: Procurement Team <procure@orbitai.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity proposal / performance guarantees

Karthik / Rishi — quick procurement clarifications from our side before we route to finance/legal: 

1) Billing for validation traffic: Orbit prefers validation traffic to be excluded from the committed usage bucket. Your note helps; please add explicit SOW language.

2) Metrics to reconcile: we want both tokens/sec and tokens-per-second-per-GPU (to account for model multiplexing). Can Redwood provide an example reconciliation export? A one-line CSV schema is fine.

3) Credits / discounts: the remedies look reasonable, but Procurement asks for a cap on total credits in year one (e.g., not to exceed one month's committed invoice). Is Redwood open to that?

4) DocuSign flow: do you sign the SOW first or the Master SaaS Agreement? We prefer MSA + SOW packaged together.

Please respond to these four and we'll move to legal review.

Procurement Team
Orbit AI
procure@orbitai.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Procurement Team <procure@orbitai.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity proposal / performance guarantees

Procurement — thanks for the questions. Inline answers and a couple of small concessions: 

> 1) Billing for validation traffic: Orbit prefers validation traffic to be excluded from the committed usage bucket.

We can accept that for this deal. Validation runs (the 72-hour soak and the three 60-minute sustained windows used for acceptance) will be excluded from committed invoicing for the first billing period. We'll add explicit SOW language: "Validation traffic executed under the dedicated acceptance test plan will be excluded from committed usage accounting for the first 30 days following the initial go-live date."

> 2) Metrics to reconcile: we want both tokens/sec and tokens-per-second-per-GPU (to account for model multiplexing). Can Redwood provide an example reconciliation export?

Yes — attached in the test plan is a sample reconciliation CSV and a short Python snippet that maps sample-level token counts to per-GPU aggregates. We will also expose a one-click export from the Console that includes: minute_ts, total_tokens, tokens_per_gpu_[id], request_count, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms.

> 3) Credits / discounts: the remedies look reasonable, but Procurement asks for a cap on total credits in year one (e.g., not to exceed one month's committed invoice). Is Redwood open to that?

We are. For Orbit we will cap cumulative credits for SLA shortfalls in year one at the monetary value of one monthly committed invoice. That will be added to the MSA/SOW.

> 4) DocuSign flow: do you sign the SOW first or the Master SaaS Agreement? We prefer MSA + SOW packaged together.

Standard Redwood practice is MSA + SOW bundled. We'll generate a single DocuSign package: MSA, SOW (including Performance Acceptance), and a 1-page exhibit describing the acceptance test steps. I will send a DocuSign link once we finalize the exact latency bands.

Operational note: we propose a kickoff window for the validation run on Mon Nov 29 — Rishi can coordinate with your SREs for the peering and test-harness setup.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
From: Jason Turner <jturner@orbitai.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity proposal / performance guarantees

Rishi / Karthik — this all looks good. Two quick items: 

- Please include in the SOW that if we exercise the 6-month reduced-rate discount (the >25% shortfall option), the discounted rate applies to committed spend only and not to any overage usage.
- Nov 29 kickoff works for our SREs; I'll have them reach out to Rishi to set exact times and exchange keys.

Assuming those minor edits, we'll get the MSA+SOW back to you for signature. Thanks for moving quickly on the credit cap and the explicit validation billing exclusion.

-Jason
Jason Turner
CTO, Orbit AI
